newsitem.title: GHANA: Malaysians take 40 pct stake in Ghana's top bank.
newsitem.headline: Malaysians take 40 pct stake in Ghana's top bank.

text.p: The Denko Industrial Corp Berhad of Malaysia has acquired a 40 percent strategic stake in Ghana's leading bank, the Ghana Commercial Bank (GCB), a senior government official said on Wednesday.

"Taking a strategic stake does not necessarily mean that you also take management, but in the case of GCB I think the Malaysians will take management," said Mercy Tetteh, chief manager of the Financial Sector Adjustment Programme Implementation Secretariat. She told Reuters the deal was concluded on Monday but declined to give other details.
Privatisation of the state-owned bank started in March with a public offer of 30 percent of its capital, which was heavily oversubscribed with 70,000 applications worth 34.3 billion cedis.
The government agreed full allotment resulting in the public holding 42 percent.
By agreeing to sell 40 percent to Denko Industrial Corp Berhad, government's stake is reduced to 18 percent.
With 568.1 billion cedis worth of assets and a 1995 net profit of 43 billion cedis, GCB is the number one commercial bank in the West African country.
Many nationalistic Ghanaians are resentful of Ghana's privatisation programme, which is part of wider donor-backed economic reforms Ghana has championed in the region for over a decade.

The government is certain to face strong criticism from such nationalists over the GCB deal, which effectively passes control of Sub-Saharan Africa's first commercial bank to foreigners. The bank was established in 1953.
